intro: Hello. Breathe in. Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour every one of them. Today's roll was seed 2857696965. Here is each roll, and what Purl made of it. You are doing amazing.

rolls.became: Purl, a ball of wool, wound tight, with one loose end it keeps tripping over. Wool has exactly one natural enemy, and it lives on the windowsill. So yes: nervous. Very.
A secondhand candle printer: a nozzle on a gantry that lays down wax one ring at a time, the way 3D printers do. It can print words into each ring. That's the whole business.
One candle. The Big Candle. Purl's logic, straight from the tape: moths go to a flame, not to wool. Build a light big enough and the moth will never look at you again.

Customers pay to have their words printed into the next ring, the way people pay for an engraved brick in a new library. You type each order on the slip (GRETA, SORRY ABOUT THE GERBIL, THE PASSWORD IS SWORDFISH) and it goes on top. On a phone, the blueprint keyboard does the same.

rolls.value: one long build that eats everything you make
rolls.became: There is no other product. Every word anyone ever types, you or the typing pool, becomes a ring of the same candle, and the elevation shows it rising out of the workshop, through the ceiling, out of the roof, past St. Giles' spire and on. The orders change as it climbs: names at the bottom, grudges at roof height, affirmations at the top.

Tape 1 of The First Billion says money is the one soft thing a moth can't eat. The top ring is always the one everybody wants, so each ring sells for a little more than the last: $1 a letter at the start, hundreds of thousands at the end. The meter is the candle's value, notched at every power of ten.

Nervous paws hit the wrong keys. The wax doesn't care why: a fumble sets a blob in the ring and it sells for half. Spellcheck Spectacles catch the first fumble on every ring, before the wax sets. The typing pool never fumbles, which Purl finds inspiring and also annoying.

Two. Gordon flutters by, Purl freezes, and the next slip is an affirmation (I AM NOT A SNACK). Type it and mean it, and a Breakthrough triples every ring for a while. And now and then the power goes out across town: everyone needs a light, there's only one candle, and every ring is worth three times as much until the lamps come back.
Dollars. A billion of them is the goal, and the candle ends up taller than a hundred metres, about twelve times as tall as it is wide.

About twenty to thirty-five minutes. The Needles (a pair of knitting needles who peck at a second keyboard) turn up in the first minute, then the spinning wheel, a punch-card Jacquard loom and a telegraph office, so the candle keeps rising while you type.

The whole game is Purl's drawing of the project: Detail A (the workshop), Detail B (the typing pool) and an elevation of the house, the town and the candle, drawn to a scale that keeps shrinking. Gordon is the only thing on the sheet in colour. Fonts: Saira Stencil One, Overpass Mono, and Nanum Pen Script for the red-pencil notes.
Thirty-two colours by NatTorpedia: blueprint blue paper and navy, sky and paper-white linework, pink red-pencil markups, cream for wax and moth, and the flame colours, saved for the end.

A kalimba rolling eighth notes in G major blues, with a hook that slides from B flat up to B, a plucked bass, then a nylon guitar and a shaker once the candle is through the roof, and a high counter-line above the town. Every typed letter is a kalimba tine climbing the same scale. In a power cut the music drops to a muffled kalimba and bass.

Purl's cassettes. "Never let a ceiling tell you where your ceiling is." "A typo is just a word on its own journey." Every upgrade is either a tape, a tool, or something from a catalogue Purl ordered by phone without asking what was on it.
Gordon, the clothes moth on the windowsill. Also St. Giles, the church whose spire the candle passes.

rolls.value: it turns out someone asked for it
rolls.became: The faded slip has been on the spike since the first day: 1 B?G L??HT. Purl filed it as junk mail. At a billion, the blueprint has one line left, WICK + LIGHTING, per ORDER #1, and the slip reads clearly: ONE BIG LIGHT, PLEASE. PRICE NO OBJECT. — G. Gordon was never after the wool. Gordon is a moth, and wanted the biggest light there could be. Gordon sat on the moth trap like a bench and pencilled itself onto the vision board the whole time.

rolls.value: an epilogue that keeps playing itself as the credits roll
rolls.became: You type BIG LIGHT. Purl gives one strand of itself for the wick and strikes the match with its eyes shut. The blueprint floods with colour, and the candle burns down by itself, ring by ring, with Gordon circling the flame, while the credits roll: the typing pool, every customer's words, Tapes 1–4, and how many wonky rings you made. Then it does it again.

outro: You are the candle. You are also the wool. Mostly the wool. Breathe.
